But the report found that much of that progress has come from growing electricity demand for air conditioning, appliances and industrial activity, rather than shifting away from reliance on coal, oil and gas.
For Southeast Asia, where electricity demand is soaring but fossil fuels remain deeply embedded in national economies, experts say accelerating that shift will be far from straightforward.
"Expanding electricity use also does not automatically translate into lower emissions unless electricity generation becomes cleaner," said Thang Nam Do, a fellow at the Australian National University's Crawford School of Public Policy.
Electrification means replacing direct fossil fuel use with electricity across transport, industrial processes and buildings. It goes well beyond electric vehicles, although those are among the most visible examples. Electric technologies - such as heat pumps and electric vehicles - convert energy into useful work far more efficiently than internal combustion engines or gas boilers, which lose most of their energy as waste heat.
"What sets this push apart is that it shifts the focus from simply generating clean power to fundamentally transforming how we consume energy across the entire economy," said Bruce Douglas, CEO of Global Renewables Alliance (GRA), a coalition of international renewable energy industry organisations.

Support for the voluntary electrification pledge has grown during COP31, with 75 countries and 94 organisations backing the initiative as of Wednesday (Nov 18), according to figures provided by the summit presidency. 
The Philippines, Singapore and Cambodia are members of the European Commission's Electrify Now coalition, which supports efforts to accelerate the use of electricity across economies.
But efforts to secure wider backing for the target have encountered resistance, with some developing countries opposing its inclusion in the summit's final declaration, according to Reuters.
Vietnam has cautioned against imposing new global targets or sector-specific emissions obligations without accounting for national circumstances, although it has not explicitly rejected the voluntary COP31 pledge.
The disagreement reflects the political divisions that have repeatedly hampered efforts to secure more ambitious emissions reduction commitments, particularly over how countries should share the burden of tackling climate change.
Coal dependence, with the fuel accounting for almost half of regional electricity generation, grid constraints and inconsistent national policies threaten to slow progress, said GRA's regional lead for Asia-Pacific, Rexor Amancio.
"I would describe Southeast Asia's progress as encouraging, but uneven, and certainly not yet at the scale required," he said.
Under existing policies, Southeast Asia's electrification share could increase to 32 per cent by 2035, according to the IEA. A more ambitious scenario outlined in its report puts it at 41 per cent.
That would require much faster adoption of electric technologies across transport, industry and buildings, alongside major investments in renewable energy, electricity grids and infrastructure to support growing demand.
Beyond being a climate commitment, the shift to electricity has also become an economic imperative, with this year's energy crisis prompting governments to reconsider their dependence on imported fuels, said Sue-Ern Tan, head of the IEA Regional Cooperation Centre in Singapore.
Around 60 per cent of Southeast Asia's crude oil imports came from the Middle East before the energy crisis, according to the IEA.
The agency projects that the region's energy import bill will reach US$160 billion in 2026, adding pressure on governments to reassess their national energy strategies, technologies and international partnerships.
"In particular, they're looking at ways to produce more energy domestically," Tan told CNA.

Related:

Heavily reliant on gas for decades, Thailand now finds it no longer cheap nor clean

‘Never encountered this before’: What an extreme El Nino means for Southeast Asia

FOSSIL FUELS DOMINATE Electricity demand in Southeast Asia has risen by more than 60 per cent since 2015, driven by growing industries, expanding cities and rising incomes. That is much faster than the region's overall energy consumption.
But many parts of national economies remain unelectrified or fuelled by dirty energy.
The transport sector is a clear example. The number of electric vehicles on the road is a visible indicator of changing technologies.
Yet while EVs accounted for around 30 per cent of new car sales in Southeast Asia in the first half of 2026, electricity supplied less than 0.5 per cent of the region's transport energy needs last year, reflecting how heavily the existing vehicle fleet still relies on oil.
Industrial processes fare better - at 29 per cent electrified - but many factories still burn coal and gas to produce heat, even though electric alternatives are already available, such as electric boilers and heat pumps.
“It's how do we deploy that more quickly across buildings, across industry and of course across transport, where there are some easy wins that can be done,” Tan said.
The IEA found that investment in switching factories to electricity has barely increased over the past decade.
"Many of these challenges are as much about governance and political economy as they are about technology," said Do.
Electrification can improve efficiency and reduce direct fuel consumption, but its overall emissions benefits depend on the electricity supply.
If an EV is charged using electricity generated by a coal-fired power plant, for example, emissions are reduced at the vehicle's tailpipe but continue to be produced elsewhere in the energy system.
The IEA reported that coal generates almost half of Southeast Asia's total electricity, while gas supplies nearly another quarter. And renewable generation would need to more than triple by 2035 to meet all additional demand in its high-electrification scenario.
Dinita Setyawati, Asia strategic impact lead at Ember, an independent global energy think tank, warned that failing to expand clean power supplies could undermine the climate benefits of electrification.
"Clean electrification is a critical catalyst for industrial transformation. But if electricity demand grows faster than renewable energy deployment, we risk locking ourselves into fossil fuel systems for decades to come," she said.

A vessel transporting coal on the Mahakam river in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, on August 7, 2023. (Photo: CNA/Danang Wisanggeni)

A REGION MOVING AT DIFFERENT SPEEDS Vietnam gets nearly 30 per cent of its final energy from electricity, the highest share in Southeast Asia, while Cambodia remains below 20 per cent.
The contrast highlights the different challenges facing countries across the region as they seek to replace fossil fuels with electricity.
It also shows there is no single path towards electrification in Southeast Asia, Do said.
“More ambitious targets are technically feasible, but achieving them will depend on investment, institutional capacity and effective implementation,” he told CNA.
Vietnam has emerged as the region’s largest electric car market, with nearly 180,000 sold in 2025, accounting for around 40 per cent of new car sales. But coal still generates almost half of the country's electricity, limiting the climate benefits of its growing use of electric power.
Indonesia, meanwhile, has competing priorities, said Fabby Tumiwa, the CEO for the Institute for Essential Services Reform, a think tank based in Jakarta.
The government is seeking to reduce its dependence on imported oil and gas by expanding the use of electricity, but its industrial development policies continue to encourage coal consumption, particularly in mineral processing and smelting.
Cheap domestic coal and subsidised gas also make it harder for factories to justify switching to electricity, he said.
Indonesia has made substantial progress in bringing electricity to households, but has been less successful in replacing fossil fuels across its wider economy. Coal supplied around 70 per cent of its electricity in 2025 and industrial coal consumption continues to grow
And the country lacks a comprehensive national electrification strategy with sector-specific targets, despite including electrification in its broader energy plans, something that could shift if the government signs onto the COP pledge in Türkiye, Fabby said.
“The technology is already there. But just through a change of policy and regulation, we can implement these kinds of electrification measures in different sectors,” he said.

Solar panels work in Quy Non, Vietnam on June 11, 2023. (AP Photo/Minh Hoang)

Elsewhere in the region, Thailand has focused on building an EV manufacturing industry, supported by government subsidies and tax incentives, while also exploring ways to replace fossil fuels in factories.
Singapore has expanded EV adoption and is planning to electrify more of its port operations, although its limited renewable energy resources remain a challenge.
The Philippines, meanwhile, faces high electricity costs and infrastructure constraints, with coal still generating nearly 60 per cent of its power.
Regional electricity integration is essential, Tan said, highlighting renewed attention on turning the ASEAN Power Grid from a long-discussed vision into actual cross-border projects, particularly ahead of Singapore's chairmanship of the regional bloc in 2027.
The grid aims to connect electricity networks across Southeast Asia, allowing countries to buy and sell power across borders, share renewable energy resources and reduce their reliance on fossil fuels. The project has made gradual progress, with nine of 18 planned cross-border electricity connections operational as of 2026.
A pilot scheme already allows Laos to export electricity to Singapore through Thailand and Malaysia, while ASEAN countries signed an enhanced agreement on Nov 15 to support further regional power trading.
But major investment and regulatory hurdles remain, with the IEA estimating that US$27 billion will be needed for planned cross-border connections by 2040.

“The reality is that Southeast Asia’s energy future is only stronger if we work together, and I think that has to continue to be a key ethos of this region,” Tan said.

Source: CNA/jb(ao)

Nov 20 : Shareholders of Australian data centre developer NextDC voted against its executive pay plans for a second year, a stock exchange filing showed on Friday, triggering a further vote on whether the entire board should be removed.
Shares of the company fell as much as 2.6 per cent to A$9.45 in early trade.
Representatives of investors who own 72.03 per cent of the company's shares voted against the remuneration report, showed the filing, which was lodged ahead of its annual meeting.
Under Australia's "two strikes" rule, a vote of 25 per cent or more against a pay report counts as a strike, and a second consecutive strike brings on a vote on whether to spill the board, meaning directors must stand for re-election.

Last year, about 72 per cent of votes were cast against the pay report, with shareholders calling for clearer accountability and greater alignment between executive rewards and returns, according to the company.
"We've carefully evaluated a broad range of shareholder feedback and responded — in our Annual Report and our recent responses to proxy advisers — to explain how our remuneration framework supports long-term shareholder value creation," Chairman Douglas Flynn said.
"We strongly believe a spill meeting would be destabilising and add cost and distraction at exactly the time when the Board and management need to focus on delivering for all shareholders."
CEO Craig Scroggie said last month that he would forgo his fiscal 2027 bonus and the company withdrew a plan to increase the non-executive directors' maximum aggregate annual remuneration by A$300,000 ($199,860.00) subject to shareholder approval.
This follows a pause in all projects lacking customer contracts after a major setback at its flagship M3 data centre in Melbourne, where the company suspended expansion over power delays and community backlash.
The same setbacks forced the firm to cut its earnings forecast and capital expenditure plans last month.
Meanwhile, NextDC lifted its annual net revenue and underlying operating earnings outlook on Friday, driven by strong sales and revenue growth outside the affected M3 contracts, alongside cost-saving measures.
($1 = 1.5011 Australian dollars)

items.title: Anthropic pulled off the biggest IPO ever. What that means, by the numbers
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: Anthropic has made a superlative-filled debut on Wall Street as it became the first major artificial intelligence lab to become a publicly traded company.
items.body: Anthropic has made a superlative-filled debut on Wall Street, breaking all records for money raised on Wall Street as it became the first major artificial intelligence lab to become a publicly traded company. The price tag on its shares was enough to put the value of the San Francisco company well beyond US$1 trillion. That kind of number was once unheard of for a company’s first moments trading on the stock market. But an acceleration in corporate wealth — and most recently the AI boom — has changed that. Anthropic is the second business to debut with a value over a trillion dollars (following SpaceX just months ago), and will join a handful of other tech giants that measure their wealth by figures reaching 13 digits. Time will tell how Anthropic ultimately fares on the public market. The Claude maker decided to proceed with its IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, fears of a possible AI bubble and growing unease among the public about the technology’s risks overall. Here are some numbers to help understand Thursday’s IPO. The amount in proceeds raised by the offering: US$81 billion That makes Anthropic’s debut the biggest ever. Ahead of trading on Thursday, it offered 980 million shares priced at US$83 each, putting Anthropic ahead of Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which set a previous record with its IPO proceeds of about US$75 billion in June. The next biggest IPO hauls went to South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (US$26.5 billion in July) and oil giant Saudi Aramco (US$25.6 billion in 2019). Anthropic’s initial valuation: US$1.5 trillion The initial price per share was set at US$83. But in early trading, that spiked more than 30 per cent — to US$111.50 a share — pushing the company’s total valuation by half a trillion dollars to US$2.01 trillion just before noon ET. By market close Thursday, Anthropic finished its first trading day at US$97.17 per share. That’s still over 17 per cent higher than its initial public offering price. In June, SpaceX ended its first day of trading on the public market with a valuation of US$2.1 trillion. Its market cap has since fallen to closer to US$1.95 trillion. Number of public companies that have reached the trillion-dollar club in the S&P 500: 11 Apple currently leads the pack at US$5.1 trillion, followed by Microsoft (US$3.8 trillion) and Nvidia (US$3.6 trillion), among others. That does not count SpaceX and Anthropic, which also have joined the trillion-dollar club even though they aren’t in the S&P 500 index yet. Only in recent memory have major corporations been valued over US$1 trillion. iPhone maker Apple was the first to pass that threshold, back in 2018. How far a trillion U.S. dollar bills would stretch if laid end to end: 93 million miles That would surpass the roughly 93 million miles (150 million kilometres) between Earth and the sun. The number “one trillion” is hard in itself for the human mind to comprehend. US$1 trillion is a thousand times greater than US$1 billion. And a million times more than US$1 million. There are more than 8.2 billion people living on Earth today, per the U.S. Census Bureau. If US$1 trillion was divided among the entire population, each person would receive almost US$122. --- Wyatte Grantham-Philips, The Associated Press

items.title: ＴＳＭＣ、中国向けＡＩ半導体の一部受注停止　米規制強化に対応
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Che Pan　Wen-Yee Lee

[１９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Che Pan　Wen-Yee Lee

[１９日 ロイター] - 半導体受託生産世界最大手の台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が、中国の人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体設計企業に対する一部の先端製品の受注を停止したことが関係者２人の話で分かった。１９日発効の米商務省による先端半導体に関連する輸出管理強化措置を踏まえた対応となる。

米商務省の新たな措置では、先端半導体は例外を除いて輸出許可が必要となる。関係者によると、ＴＳＭＣは顧客が米国の輸出許可を取得しない限り、１６ナノメートル以下の製造プロセスを用いる製品の受注を停止するよう指示した。主要なＡＩ半導体の多くは、７ナノ以下のプロセスで製造されているが、中国の設計企業に供給するものは、高度なパッケージングを必要としない２８ナノや４０ナノといった旧世代技術を用いた製品に事実上制限されるとみられる。

ＴＳＭＣの対応は、顧客の事業拠点や親会社、主要株主、パッケージング業者、輸送ルートでもより厳格な審査を求めており、海外子会社や仲介業者を通じて発注された注文も対象に含めるという。

一部の中国企業が個別の輸出許可なしに高性能ＡＩプロセッサーを生産するためのルートが閉ざされ、国産代替品の開発に向けた中国当局の取り組みにも影響する可能性がある。

items.title: トランプ氏、イランへの攻撃再開巡る判断は来年に持ち越し　「急がず」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Steve Holland

[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Steve Holland

[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１９日、イランへの大規模攻撃を再開するかどうかの判断を来年に持ち越す考えを示した。これまでは今月初旬の米中間選挙後に判断を下す可能性を示唆していた。

トランプ大統領はロイターとのインタビューで、イランへの新たな攻撃の可能性について、「それについては年明けに話そう」と述べた。

中国訪問を終えてワシントンに戻る機中で、「われわれには時間がある」と語った。

１９日に放映されたＦＯＸニュースとのインタビューでも、イラン情勢を巡り「１月１日以降どうなるか見てみよう」と発言。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスとのインタビューでは、「イランに関する決定を急いで下すつもりはない」との認識を示した。

２０２８年大統領選の候補となる可能性があるバンス副大統領は、イラン戦争が共和党の中間選挙惨敗を招いたと批判し、トランプ氏と公に距離を置いた。トランプ氏はその後、バンス氏にイランを巡る外交活動から離れ、代わりに国内問題に注力するよう指示した。

トランプ氏はロイターの取材に対し、「ＪＤ（バンス氏）の発言に問題はなかった」と述べた。「彼の言ったことは正しかった。この状況全体が、選挙がわれわれの思い通りにいかなかった理由の一つであることは確かだと、彼は言った」と回答。「そして重要なのは、もう一度やり直すとしても同じことをするかということだ。答えはイエスだ。イランに核兵器を持たせるわけにはいかないからだ」と述べた。

トランプ氏はまた、ＦＯＸニュースのインタビューで、イランが米首都ワシントンで放射性物質を飛散させる『ダーティーボム（汚い爆弾）』による攻撃を計画している可能性があるとした今週のＣＮＮ報道について、「イランがガス兵器や生物兵器を検討している兆候がある。われわれが核兵器の保有を阻止してきたためだ」と述べた。ただ、ワシントン市民は警戒すべきかとの質問には、「そうは思わない」と答え、イランの脅威を差し迫ったものとはみていない姿勢を示した。

items.title: Anthropic set to begin trading as a US$1.5-trillion company in the biggest IPO on record
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: Anthropic is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its IPO at US$83 per share, valuing the artificial intelligence giant at $1.5 trillion and surpassing SpaceX as the largest ...
items.body: NEW YORK — The artificial intelligence giant Anthropic opened for trading Thursday in the biggest public stock offering ever, despite investor fears of a possible AI bubble and public anxiety that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods. Anthropic shares began trading at US$111.50, spiking more than 30 per cent above the initial public offering price, before closing at US$97.17, more than 17 per cent higher than the IPO. A day earlier, the company priced its IPO at US$83 per share, enough to value the entire business at US$1.5 trillion, surpassing SpaceX as the largest IPO on record. At the start of trading, the valuation leaped to US$2.01 trillion. The initial price was surprisingly high given that investor worries had ratcheted up even more recently following the stunning ouster of AI’s chief promoter, the CEO of Nvidia, in a possible Chinese spying scandal. Anthropic had earlier set a much lower price range between US$70 to US$78 per share. “It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.” A big test remains if investors maintain the classic “IPO pop” by keeping the stock aloft in its first day — or if it will tumble by the close. The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool offered 980 million shares to the public, which at US$83 per share translated into proceeds of US$81 billion. Anthropic’s soaring debut on Wall Street was not enough to carry the rest of the market. U.S. stock indexes fell after a morning rally quickly evaporated. IPO offers a way to raise money without going deeper into debt In addition to market jitters over AI, the IPO is facing down a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. For its part, Anthropic rival OpenAI decided to postpone its initial offering until next year. The company, trading under the ticker symbol ANT, is also facing big financial challenges ahead. Anthropic already has taken on US$6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial.” Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to pay interest and principal are limited. While the company showed ample cash in its last financial report, it would have likely run through it quickly given its outsize spending plans. In the same financial report, the company said it had signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend US$900 billion on computing power and infrastructure in the coming years, including US$70 billion in the next 12 months. Such massive spending by AI companies, comparable to the Gilded Age splurge on railroads, have scared lenders, helping to push borrowing rates high recently. With the IPO, though, Anthropic will now have enormous resources to accelerate its expansion without taking on more debt. The offering will also allow its employees to sell vested stock, making many of them millionaires overnight — and potentially adding billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei. AI industry faces concerns about data centres, a possible bubble and regulations Founded five years ago by the siblings along with several other former OpenAI veterans, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company. But both companies have plenty of other competitors, including Google, startups in the U.S. and China and SpaceX, which has an AI business. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all lost more money than they’ve made because of the huge costs associated with building AI. That has fueled growing concerns about a bubble forming in the sector. Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned, AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the internet within months. In comments at the opening bell Thursday, Amodei sought to dampen fears by stressing a commitment to ensure humans are in control of the technology. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same,” he said. ”The goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.” Amid mounting fears, the regulatory environment could change for Anthropic once the new Congress is in session. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry as a backlash unfolds against data centres. And two big states offering incentives for data centres, Texas and Georgia, just elected Democratic governors who have vowed to stop new construction. In his comments Thursday, Amodei also touted a range of positive uses for AI, noting that Claude already is helping scientists do quicker research and that the technology could help accelerate that progress in the future. “Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox and polio history for most of the world,” he said, “but progress in other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families.” He also pointed to Claude’s use across companies, nonprofits and government services. “I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future,” he said. Adding to the pressure to go public was the possibility that demand for AI shares could drop or even collapse. Investors have become anxious about the massive financing needs of the sector, and several tech companies have pulled IPO plans recently. Market valuation for AI companies is going to be “up and down for many years to come, but more up than down,” said Rich Lesser, the global chair and former CEO of Boston Consulting Group. “Exactly what the flow of that will be, it’s very hard to predict,” Lesser said Tuesday in an interview with The Associated Press at the Semafor Silicon Valley & the World forum. “There’s no question what Anthropic and OpenAI and Google and a number of the other players in this industry have done is pretty remarkable.” ___ Bernard Condon and Barbara Ortutay, The Associated Press Ortutay reported from Oakland, California. Associated Press business writers Kaitlyn Huamani in Los Angeles and Michelle Chapman in New York contributed.

items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが主要通貨バスケットに対して小幅上昇し、足元の上昇基調を延長した。リスク選好が後退し、アンソロピック
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが主要通貨バスケットに対して小幅上昇し、足元の上昇基調を延長した。リスク選好が後退し、アンソロピック の超大型新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）も人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る熱狂の薄れに歯止めをかけられなかった。

ドルは特に新興国通貨に対して強含んだ。

コーペイのチーフマーケットストラテジスト、カール・シャモッタ氏は「ドルの流動性確保に向けた争奪戦が起きており、世界的に金融環境が引き締まる中で新興国市場全体が深刻な売りに見舞われている」と述べた。

ただ、一部のストラテジストは、新たな材料がなければ短期的にドルがこれ以上大きく上昇するとの見方に懐疑的だった。

ドル指数は０．１％高の１０３．８８となった。

ドル／円は０．２％高の１５９．６１５円と、４営業日続いた下落に歯止めがかかった。

リスクに敏感な豪ドルはこの日０．７％下落した。オーストラリアの１０月の雇用者数は２カ月連続で減少し、失業率は５年ぶりの高水準に上昇。豪金利はピークに達した可能性が高いとの見方を強めた。

三菱ＵＦＪフィナンシャル・グループ（ＭＵＦＧ）のシニア通貨アナリスト、リー・ハードマン氏は「ＦＲＢの利上げ観測が急速にタカ派方向に織り込み直されたことが、コモディティー価格や関連通貨の軟調さの一因となっている」と述べた。

暗号資産（仮想通貨）のビットコインは約１％安の６万１９８５ドルとなり、４カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。

items.title: 米国株式市場＝主要3指数2％超安、アンソロピック上場でもＡＩ熱戻らず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は急落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックがナスダック市場に新規上場したものの、冷え込むＡＩ投資熱を再び高めることはできず、同社株は序盤の高値から上げ幅を縮小した。

主要株価３指数がいずれも２％超下落し、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種は６営業日続落した。

過去最大の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）となったアンソロピックの初値は１１１．５０ドルと、公開価格の８３ドルを約３４％上回った。時価総額は一時２兆ドルを超えたが、その後は勢いが鈍り、公開価格を１７．１％上回る水準で取引を終えた。

アージェント・キャピタルのポートフォリオマネジャー、ジェド・エラーブルック氏は「アンソロピックのＩＰＯは非常に大きな注目を集めている」と指摘。「その資金はどこかから来ている。投資家はアンソロピックを組み入れるためにポートフォリオを調整しているので、きょうの値動きが上向きであれ下向きであれ、そこにあまり多くの意味を読み取るべきではない」と述べた。

その上で「データセンター設備投資の伸びに対する私の見方は、この１─２カ月でやや後退した。エヌビディアの危機的状況は大きな問題だ。中間選挙も影響を及ぼしている」とし、「データセンターの建設費用は高くなり、建設ペースは遅くなるだろう」と述べた。

アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（ＡＭＤ）は７．７％急落。調査報道メディアのハンターブルックは、系列ファンドのハンターブルック・キャピタルが同社株の空売りポジションを取ったと伝えた。

ハイテク株は大半が下落し、マイクロンとブロードコムはいずれも２．１％安となった。エヌビディアは３．３％下落し、６営業日続落。

ネオクラウド（新興クラウド事業者）のコアウィーブは６．１％、ネビウスは９．４％、それぞれ下落した。

一方、サイバーセキュリティー企業のパロアルトネットワークスは６．４％上昇。２０２７年の売上高見通しを引き上げたことを好感した。

小売り大手ウォルマートは１．０％安。通期売上高見通しが市場予想を下回った。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を４．３７対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも３．５５対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は２０８億３０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１９０億株。

items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は急落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックがナス...
items.body:
米国株式市場＝主要3指数2％超安、アンソロピック上場でもＡＩ熱戻らず
6:28 配信

11月18日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）で撮影。REUTERS/Brendan McDermid（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は急落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックがナスダック市場に新規上場したものの、冷え込むＡＩ投資熱を再び高めることはできず、同社株は序盤の高値から上げ幅を縮小した。

主要株価３指数がいずれも２％超下落し、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種は６営業日続落した。

過去最大の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）となったアンソロピックの初値は１１１．５０ドルと、公開価格の８３ドルを約３４％上回った。時価総額は一時２兆ドルを超えたが、その後は勢いが鈍り、公開価格を１７．１％上回る水準で取引を終えた。

アージェント・キャピタルのポートフォリオマネジャー、ジェド・エラーブルック氏は「アンソロピックのＩＰＯは非常に大きな注目を集めている」と指摘。「その資金はどこかから来ている。投資家はアンソロピックを組み入れるためにポートフォリオを調整しているので、きょうの値動きが上向きであれ下向きであれ、そこにあまり多くの意味を読み取るべきではない」と述べた。

その上で「データセンター設備投資の伸びに対する私の見方は、この１─２カ月でやや後退した。エヌビディアの危機的状況は大きな問題だ。中間選挙も影響を及ぼしている」とし、「データセンターの建設費用は高くなり、建設ペースは遅くなるだろう」と述べた。

アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（ＡＭＤ）は７．７％急落。調査報道メディアのハンターブルックは、系列ファンドのハンターブルック・キャピタルが同社株の空売りポジションを取ったと伝えた。

ハイテク株は大半が下落し、マイクロンとブロードコムはいずれも２．１％安となった。エヌビディアは３．３％下落し、６営業日続落。

ネオクラウド（新興クラウド事業者）のコアウィーブは６．１％、ネビウスは９．４％、それぞれ下落した。

一方、サイバーセキュリティー企業のパロアルトネットワークスは６．４％上昇。２０２７年の売上高見通しを引き上げたことを好感した。

小売り大手ウォルマートは１．０％安。通期売上高見通しが市場予想を下回った。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を４．３７対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも３．５５対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は２０８億３０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１９０億株。

items.author: CNA
items.summary: Her ex-husband, Philip Young, admitted to more than 50 offences, including rape and sharing recordings of the abuse online.
items.body:

Four men guilty of sex crimes against woman drugged by husband in UK case with echoes of Pelicot

Her ex-husband, Philip Young, admitted to more than 50 offences, including rape and sharing recordings of the abuse online.

Joanne Young looks on outside Winchester Crown Court after a jury returned guilty verdicts in the case of all four men accused of raping or sexually abusing her while she was drugged by her then-husband between 2016 and 2023, in Winchester, Britain, November 19, 2026. FAST

WINCHESTER: Four British men were convicted on Thursday (Nov 19) of raping or sex ually abusing a woman who was drugged by her then- husband in a case with echoes of that of Gisele Pelicot , the French woman who became a global symbol in the fight against sex ual violence.
Joanne Young, like Pelicot , decided to waive her legal right to anonymity after discovering that her husband at the time had repeatedly drugged her and advertised her for sex online to strangers over more than a decade.
Philip Young, a 50-year-old former local councillor, pleaded guilty in January to more than 50 charges against his ex-wife, including 11 counts of rape and charges relating to recording the abuse and publishing it online hundreds of times.
"This abuse has cost me my life as I knew it," Joanne Young said outside court. "The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way."

CALL TO RECONSIDER LAW ON CONSENT Police discovered the abuse only after an account linked to Philip Young posted bestiality images online in 2024 and then seized his devices, containing videos and images of the abuse.
Young's crimes have striking similarities to those of Dominique Pelicot , who admitted drugging his then-wife Gisele and inviting dozens of men to rape her, prompting a 2024 trial that horrified the world and spurred France to revamp its rape law.
Britain's National Crime Agency said this year it had uncovered a "truly international network" of drug-facilitated rape and sex ual assault, which it said was organised online and had members across the world.
Law enforce men t officials from 10 countries, including the US, are now working on a global operation to target drug-facilitated sex ual assaults.
Joanne Young said her case "raises serious questions about how the law deals with consent", adding: "I urge the govern men t to look at this as a priority so that wo men are properly protected in the future."

Women's rights campaigners outside Winchester Crown Court, where a jury is deliberating in the case of four men accused of raping or sexually assaulting Joanne Young, in Winchester, Britain, Nov 13, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

FIFTH MAN HAD PLEADED GUILTY The men found guilty following a trial at Winchester Crown Court, in southern England, had responded to adverts posted by Philip Young, who admitted drugging his wife and inviting strangers to have sex with her, watching and filming while it happened.
Richard Clive Wilkins, 62, was convicted of rape and assault by penetration, Norman Macksoni, 48, was also convicted of rape, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, was found guilty of sex ual assault and assault by penetration, while Mohammed Hassan, 38, was convicted of one count of sex ual assault.
In defences echoing those of many of the 50 co-defendants of Dominique Pelicot who were convicted in France, they said they thought Joanne Young consented and that it was a shared fantasy with her then- husband .
She had sat in court as prosecutor Sarah Jones said her ex- husband had posted images online, showing his then-wife tied to her bed and blindfolded, as he "sought strangers to come and sleep with his wife – any age, any race".
After the verdicts were announced, Judge Pushpinder Saini said she had shown "amazing bravery".
A fifth man, Dean Hamilton, 47, had previously admitted rape, assault by penetration and sex ual assault.
All five, along with Philip Young, will be sentenced next month and Saini said they faced a significant custodial sentence.

PELICOT NOT AN ISOLATED CASE The Pelicot trial horrified the world, but it now appears to be far from an isolated case .
Specialist Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor James Foster said the case "marks the first time in England that a jury has convicted men of sex ually assaulting a woman , who had been drugged in abuse organised by her husband ".
In April, law enforce men t bodies from 10 countries, coordinated by Europol, the EU's law enforce men t agency, set up "Project Medusa" to tackle the issue, led by investigators from Britain and Germany, and including the US, France and Canada.
Those involved have since launched 113 investigations linked to that operation, leading to 57 arrests and 158 safeguarded victims, Europol said in June.
The Crown Prosecution Service said British police had spoken with investigators who worked on the Pelicot case and that the toxicology expert whose evidence was used in France had also worked on the case involving Joanne Young.
"I live with a pain that's hard to put into words ... it is terrifying that this could happen to anyone," Young said.

Source: Reuters/fs

Nov 19 : Intuit said on Thursday it has agreed to sell email marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times more in its largest deal ever.
Shares of the TurboTax maker were down 10 per cent after the bell, while those of Bending Spoons shares rose 3 per cent.
Intuit said the sale will sharpen its focus on AI-powered products for small businesses, and that it plans to use the cash proceeds to repurchase shares.
The company has increasingly focused on integrating artificial intelligence across its products as it seeks to automate tasks for consumers and businesses and expand the range of services it provides.

The deal includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in stock, and is expected to close in early 2027.
Intuit acquired Mailchimp in 2021 for about $12 billion, bringing the email marketing platform into its small-business software portfolio.
The deal gives Bending Spoons, which went public in July, another major digital business to add to its growing portfolio. The company said it plans to invest substantially in the marketing platform and pursue changes to its technology, products, marketing and monetization.
"Mailchimp has helped millions of businesses grow and acquire customers through email marketing automation," said Jack Tam, senior vice president at Intuit.
Intuit said that revenue from Mailchimp decreased 1 per cent to $313 million in the first quarter.
It also trimmed 2027 forecast and now expects full-year revenue to grow 8 per cent to 9 per cent, compared with its previous forecast for 9 per cent to 10 per cent growth.
Intuit said the revised guidance reflects a change to its personal-finance platform Credit Karma, which has seen performance fall below expectations as higher interest rates weighed on growth and a shift in consumer behavior had a faster-than-anticipated impact on the business.
The company maintained its full-year operating income and profit guidance.

By Steve Holland
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) – US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he was looking to next year before deciding on renewed strikes against Iran, pushing back a timeline he had previously tied to this month’s midterm elections.

Asked about the possibility of new Iran strikes, Trump told Reuters in an interview: “Well, I’ll talk to you about it after the beginning of the year.”

In recent weeks, Trump has alternated between threats of escalation against Iran and indicating he could wind down hostilities, with the two sides in a standoff over efforts to resolve the conflict. 

Show Full Article

Trump spoke from his plane as he returned to Washington on Thursday from his trip to China.

While there, he also told Fox News in an interview that aired on Thursday: “We’ll see what happens after January 1.” He also cited the new timeline in a separate interview on Thursday with a reporter for Axios and Israel’s News 12, saying: “I’m not rushing to make any decisions on Iran.”

In the weeks leading up to the November 3 congressional contests, Trump repeatedly suggested that Iran would be more willing to strike a deal in the eight-month conflict after the US elections.

But after his fellow Republicans lost both chambers of Congress, his administration last week said it believes its blockade and economic sanctions against Iran are working. The US Senate, which Republicans control until January 3, again on Thursday rejected a measure aimed at curbing the war.

Trump has acknowledged Iran played a role in the losses but has said he would not have changed course, adding that he would hold off on fresh strikes for now.

Vice President JD Vance, a possible 2028 presidential candidate, publicly distanced himself from the war, which he blamed for the party’s political rout. Trump later directed Vance away from Iran diplomatic efforts to instead focus on domestic matters.

Thursday’s joint statement issued following Trump’s summit with his Russian and Chinese counterparts did not mention the conflict with Iran.

DOWNPLAYS BOMB THREAT

Trump, on Fox News, was also asked about a report carried by CNN this week that Iran was planning to detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington. A dirty bomb uses conventional explosives to spread radioactive material.

He appeared to downplay such a threat, saying “I don’t think so” when asked if people in the capital should be alarmed, although he also said there were indications Iran was “looking at” biological or chemical weapons, without elaborating.

“There is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio, because we’ve shut them out with the nuclear. Nuclear is much harder. And they’re looking at gas and … biological weapons — not nice — and other things,” Trump said.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry, in a post on X, said US accusations about Tehran developing chemical and biological weapons were intended to create fear and justify military action. It earlier this week called the CNN report “baseless”.

Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, which Tehran denies. Destroying Iran’s nuclear programme was one of Trump’s main justifications when he launched strikes against Iran in February alongside Israel.

The head of Israel’s Mossad spy agency also advocated for a resumption of joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran in a visit to the US this month, Reuters reported earlier.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also said he did not think there was any imminent threat to the US capital.

AI surge could strain US capacity and overheat economy, Fed's Goolsbee says

Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee participates in a session titled "The Future of Global Finance" during the Semafor World Economy conference in Washington, D.C., U.S., April 14, 2026. REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

WASHINGTON, Nov 19 : The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock.
"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python."
Goolsbee said he sees the multitrillion-dollar pipeline of data-center projects already adding to what he referred to as "borderline, disturbingly high inflation rates" that are well above the Fed's 2 per cent target and potentially heading higher.
He said he felt the Anthropic IPO, giving the company's early shareholders the ability to tap equity holdings well in excess of $1 trillion, could on its own become relevant to the path of the broader economy.

"A $1.5 trillion IPO. The question of what people are going to do with the money now that they have some access to that liquidity is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," Goolsbee said. "We're watching that."
DATA-CENTER BACKLASH
The US central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point at its December 8-9 meeting. Fed policymakers also are wrestling with how the AI boom is influencing the economy.
The recent US midterm elections saw AI skepticism emerge at the polls, with municipalities in a number of states approving ballot initiatives that could limit how quickly and where data centers get built, potentially slowing the industry's breakneck evolution.
At the same time, the Fed this week held a high-level conference looking at the possible impact on productivity and the labor market should the new technologies diffuse through the economy and reach a potential that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has characterized as pivotal to US economic leadership.
In remarks at an earlier event on Thursday, Goolsbee said it was not yet clear what effect AI will have on productivity or the economy's underlying potential, noting that it took years — even decades — for other general-purpose technologies to change how businesses operated on a broad basis.
In the meantime, the Fed will have to cope with short-term effects that so far seem to be inflationary.
"The Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy," with monetary policy set tight enough to keep demand and supply in balance, Goolsbee said at the event.
The Chicago Fed chief did not say if he would support a larger half-percentage-point rate hike at the December meeting, as at least one of his colleagues has advocated, but added that all options were on the table.
"The question of how steep the rate path is going to be and if there will be any rate increases should be determined, in my view, by whether you think inflation is going to be heading back to 2 per cent on its own or not," Goolsbee said. "The evidence does not suggest we're on a path back to 2 per cent."

Source: Reuters

MOGADISHU, Nov 19 (Reuters) – Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador on Thursday to leave the country within 72 hours and withdrew its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Emirates of unspecified violations of Somalia’s sovereignty that amounted to an “open invasion”.

“Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia,” Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency.

“All Somalis are urged to defend their country and unite against the open invasion of the UAE against the sovereignty, security, land and unity of Somalis.”

Show Full Article

The minister did not elaborate on the actions the UAE had taken that had provoked Somalia’s response. In a speech on Tuesday, Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud had accused the UAE of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments to oppose the federal government.

The UAE, which has helped fund and train Somalia’s military in the past and has backed ports and other commercial ventures there, has long denied meddling in the country’s affairs.

The UAE denounced what it called the Somali government’s “escalatory and hostile” approach towards it on Thursday, its foreign ministry spokesperson said.

The UAE foreign ministry, in a statement, expressed regret over what it described as the Somali government’s attempts to drag the UAE into its internal power struggles, saying such actions could harm the interests of both countries.

The ministry said the UAE had closed its embassy in Mogadishu and withdrawn its diplomatic staff in January 2026 over what it described as hostile actions by the Somali government, including the cancellation of bilateral agreements.

It reaffirmed the UAE’s commitment to maintaining and strengthening ties with the Somali people.

In January, Somalia said it had ended all agreements with the United Arab Emirates, including port deals and defence and security cooperation, accusing the UAE of undermining its national sovereignty.

Three self-governing Somali regions that have close relations with the United Arab Emirates dismissed that move at the time.

The UAE has long leveraged its wealth to expand its influence across the Horn of Africa, using a mix of economic, military and diplomatic clout to assert regional power.

For decades Somalia’s federal government has had only limited authority across the country, and has failed to defeat Islamist militants, despite years of international support, including African peacekeepers and US air strikes.

The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018, and still covers salaries and provides logistics for around 3,400 Somali military police and special forces troops in and around the capital, according to senior Somali sources.

It has also forged bonds directly with regional governments, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure on the coast along global shipping routes.

(Reporting by Abdi Sheikh, additionral reporting by Yomna Ehab and Ahmed Tolba; Writing by George Obulutsa; Editing by Toby Chopra, Peter Graff and Chizu Nomiyama )

items.body:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞　続落して取引を終えた。投資家のリスク回避の姿勢が強く、幅広い銘柄が売られた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４日続落し、終値として約１カ月半ぶりの安値を付けた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．７１％安と、６営業日続落した。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックが大型新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を果たす中でも、ＡＩを巡る投資家の懸念が続いた。 日用品のユニリーバは２．２％、電力・ガス供給のナショナル・グリッドは２．６％、通信大手のボーダフォンは４．０％、石油大手のシェルは０．６％、金融大手ＨＳＢＣは０．９％、製薬大手ＧＳＫは１．７％いずれも値下がりした。金融のクローズ・ブラザーズ・グループは７．７％下落した。一方、増益決算を発表した防衛機器バブコック・インターナショナルは９．４％高だった。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　４日続落して取引を終えた。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は終値として約１カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。食品・飲料やヘルスケア株などの売り注文が目立った。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックの大型新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）が注目される中、ＡＩを巡る懸念から投資家のリスク回避の姿勢が強まっている。 ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種食品・飲料株指数は２．０５％、ヘルスケア株指数は１．７９％それぞれ下落した。スイスの製薬大手ノバルティスは３．２％安。中期の売上高目標を従来予想の下限としたことが売り材料視された。米企業の買収を検討していると報じられたフランスの製薬大手サノフィは２．９％下落した。オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは２．２％、欧州の半導体大手ＳＴマイクロエレクトロニクスは１．６％、ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは０．３％それぞれ上昇。業績見通しが市場予想を上回ったフランスの半導体材料大手ソイテックは１２．０％高だった。イタリアの銀行大手ウニクレディトは、０．２％高。ドイツのコメルツ銀行買収に関する主要な争点でドイツ政府と合意した。一方、コメルツ銀は１．２％下落した。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　域内国債利回りが小幅に上昇した。エネルギー価格が上昇したことが背景。市場はこの日に新規上場した米アンソロピックの動向を注視している。ドイツ１０年債利回りは２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し、３．４１％となった。独２年債利回りは３ｂｐ上昇し、３．１５％となった。ユーロ圏の指標となる独１０年債利回りは、９月下旬に１７年ぶりの高水準となる３．６５３％を付けた後、ここ数カ月は低下している。エネルギー価格が落ち着いたほか、ハイテク株の売りを受け、投資家が安全資産に資金を移したことが背景にある。１９日は欧州の天然ガス価格が約３％上昇し、国債利回りを押し上げた。原油価格も小幅に上昇した。過去最大となったアンソロピックの新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）は、株式市場全体をほとんど押し上げず、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種指数は小幅に下落した。このため、安全資産とされる債券に投資資金が向かい、利回りの上昇は抑えられた。フランス１０年債利回りは１９日、５ｂｐ上昇して４．９４％となり、独仏１０年債利回り格差は１５３ｂｐとなった。

items.body:
欧州市場サマリー（19日）
5:26 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞　続落して取引を終えた。投資家のリスク回避の姿勢が強く、幅広い銘柄が売られた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４日続落し、終値として約１カ月半ぶりの安値を付けた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．７１％安と、６営業日続落した。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックが大型新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を果たす中でも、ＡＩを巡る投資家の懸念が続いた。 日用品のユニリーバは２．２％、電力・ガス供給のナショナル・グリッドは２．６％、通信大手のボーダフォンは４．０％、石油大手のシェルは０．６％、金融大手ＨＳＢＣは０．９％、製薬大手ＧＳＫは１．７％いずれも値下がりした。金融のクローズ・ブラザーズ・グループは７．７％下落した。一方、増益決算を発表した防衛機器バブコック・インターナショナルは９．４％高だった。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　４日続落して取引を終えた。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は終値として約１カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。食品・飲料やヘルスケア株などの売り注文が目立った。人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックの大型新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）が注目される中、ＡＩを巡る懸念から投資家のリスク回避の姿勢が強まっている。 ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種食品・飲料株指数は２．０５％、ヘルスケア株指数は１．７９％それぞれ下落した。スイスの製薬大手ノバルティスは３．２％安。中期の売上高目標を従来予想の下限としたことが売り材料視された。米企業の買収を検討していると報じられたフランスの製薬大手サノフィは２．９％下落した。オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは２．２％、欧州の半導体大手ＳＴマイクロエレクトロニクスは１．６％、ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは０．３％それぞれ上昇。業績見通しが市場予想を上回ったフランスの半導体材料大手ソイテックは１２．０％高だった。イタリアの銀行大手ウニクレディトは、０．２％高。ドイツのコメルツ銀行買収に関する主要な争点でドイツ政府と合意した。一方、コメルツ銀は１．２％下落した。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　域内国債利回りが小幅に上昇した。エネルギー価格が上昇したことが背景。市場はこの日に新規上場した米アンソロピックの動向を注視している。ドイツ１０年債利回りは２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し、３．４１％となった。独２年債利回りは３ｂｐ上昇し、３．１５％となった。ユーロ圏の指標となる独１０年債利回りは、９月下旬に１７年ぶりの高水準となる３．６５３％を付けた後、ここ数カ月は低下している。エネルギー価格が落ち着いたほか、ハイテク株の売りを受け、投資家が安全資産に資金を移したことが背景にある。１９日は欧州の天然ガス価格が約３％上昇し、国債利回りを押し上げた。原油価格も小幅に上昇した。過去最大となったアンソロピックの新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）は、株式市場全体をほとんど押し上げず、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種指数は小幅に下落した。このため、安全資産とされる債券に投資資金が向かい、利回りの上昇は抑えられた。フランス１０年債利回りは１９日、５ｂｐ上昇して４．９４％となり、独仏１０年債利回り格差は１５３ｂｐとなった。

FAST

Nov 19 : Meta Platforms plans to price its pocket-sized AI device, Muse Charm, at $300 and offer buyers up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon, the Information reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter.
• Verizon did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment, while a Meta spokesperson said "we're charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we'll have more to share soon"
• The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference
• Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform

• Users can tap the gadget to access Muse directly, bypassing AI apps on their smartphones
• The device features a roughly 2-inch (5-cm) screen that can be navigated with a thumb, with a customizable Muse character at its center
• A built-in 5G modem allows access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though it cannot make call
• Muse has gained traction among users as Meta expands its push to make its AI assistant a more widely used consumer service
• The AI agent allows users to delegate tasks such as shopping, travel booking and form-filling to an AI agent
• Meta is expected to launch Charm in time for the holiday shopping season in December, according to Zuckerberg's comments at the company's Connect event.

items.title: 欧州、頭越しのウクライナ和平容認せず　「ヤルタ方式」に批判
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
James Mackenzie　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
James Mackenzie　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン １９日 ロイター] - 欧州の同盟国は１９日、ウクライナを支援するためベルリンで会合を開き、自らの頭越しに和平を決める試みがあれば容認しないと警告した。トランプ米大統領が中国の習近平国家主席との首脳会談の場でロシアのプーチン大統領を「友人」として歓待する中での会合だった。

この日、「有志連合」の会合には、ドイツ、フランス、英国、ポーランド、イタリアの首脳と北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の首脳に加え、米政権のウィットコフ特使とトランプ氏の娘婿クシュナー氏も参加した。

ドイツ、フランス、英国、ウクライナの首脳は会合後に発表した共同声明で、ロシアがウクライナの主要な同盟国による揺るぎない支援に持ちこたえることはできないと表明した。

プーチン氏が深センでの首脳会談で外交的な成功を収めたことから、ウクライナと欧州大陸の将来を左右する決定が欧州の関与なしに下されかねないとの欧州の懸念が浮き彫りになった。

深センでの会談は、米国、英国、ソ連による１９４５年のヤルタ会談になぞらえられた。ヤルタ会談は勢力圏を公式に定め、大国が小国に押し付ける取引の代名詞となった。

ドイツのメルツ首相は「『ヤルタ』方式は平和をもたらさない」と一蹴。記者団に対し、各国首脳は欧州が分割されるのを許さないだろうと付け加えた。メルツ氏はまた、深センでの首脳会談は単に「写真撮影の機会」にすぎないと批判した上で、「米国は、われわれ抜きでは平和はあり得ないと理解している。われわれも、米国が味方にいれば平和の見通しが高まることを分かっている」と述べた。

トランプ氏は会合に電話で参加した。大統領専用機内からロイターの取材に応じ、参加者に伝えた内容について「プーチン大統領は合意を望んでいる。誰もが合意を望んでいるのだから、合意しよう、ということだ」と語った。

また、４年半に及ぶ戦争への欧州の支出について参加者に不満を述べたとの見方を否定し、「合意を結んで、その資金を自国のために使うべきだ。もうその時だ」と伝えたと説明した。 

メルツ氏と並んで立ったクシュナー氏は同盟国を安心させようと腐心し、トランプ氏は欧州を味方につけた和平合意を望んでおり、ロシアは欧州との多国間協議に応じることに同意したと強調した。

クシュナー氏によると、トランプ氏は、プーチン、習両氏との会談を終えて「平和は達成可能だ」と考えるに至った。

クシュナー氏はまた、トランプ氏はＮＡＴＯの集団防衛を定めた第５条に基づくウクライナへの安全の保証の提供に前向きで、ロシアもそれに「違和感を覚えなくなった」と述べた。

ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、今後の和平交渉には欧州を加えなければならないと述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏はその後、記者団に対し、ＮＡＴＯ第５条に基づく安全の保証がどのように機能するのかは明確でないと述べた。

＜「プーチン氏は友人ではない」＞

トランプ氏とプーチン氏の会談は、欧州の同盟国と米民主党の反発を招いた。

ポーランドのトゥスク首相は「プーチン氏はわれわれの友人ではないし、決して友人にはならないだろう」と述べた。

デンマークのフレデリクセン首相も記者団に「米大統領がプーチン大統領と席を同じくしたがることが、私には全く理解できない」と厳しく批判。プーチン氏は「今日の会談でさらに勢いづくだろう。彼は満足げに見える」と警告した。

記者から、首脳会談でトランプ氏がプーチン氏を「私の友人」と呼んで出迎えたことについて問われると、ゼレンスキー氏は肩をすくめて立ち去った。

一方、ＮＡＴＯのルッテ事務総長は主要な核保有国同士が会談するのは普通のことだと指摘。「トランプ大統領はウクライナでの平和を実現するため、絶えず超人的な努力を重ねてきた。私はただそれを称賛するばかりだ」と述べた。ルッテ氏はＮＡＴＯ内の緊張を和らげ、トランプ氏をつなぎ留めようと繰り返し努めてきた経緯がある。

TOKYO, Nov 20 : Japanese investors sought to buy more than 1.5 trillion yen ($9.40 billion) worth of Anthropic shares at its public listing this week, two people familiar with the offer said.
Japanese investors ultimately secured $2.98 billion worth of the shares, a filing showed on Thursday.
Anthropic raised $81 billion in total worldwide in what became the world's largest initial public offering on record, eclipsing SpaceX, which raised $75 billion at its listing in June.
Market sentiment has turned against AI-related firms in recent months, which sparked speculation that the Claude developer's listing would struggle to win over investors.

Anthropic ultimately priced its offering at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78.
Some Japanese investors saw Anthropic as the frontrunner among AI firms and so justified large orders, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the IPO publicly.
Other investors sought smaller allocations or sat out the offering altogether, seeing greater prospective returns in semiconductor stocks that have fallen sharply, such as Nvidia and Kioxia, or in waiting for OpenAI’s listing due next year, one of the people said.
More than 1,000 individuals sought allotments over 100 million yen, according to a demand survey by Mizuho Securities, part of Mizuho Financial Group, which was among the underwriters of the IPO and arranged the sale of the majority of shares sold in Japan. These applications totalled around 200 billion yen, the survey showed.
($1 = 159.5700 yen)

items.title: New York City Horse-Carriage Ban Unconstitutional, Lawsuit Says
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: New York City’s brand new law banning horse-drawn carriages is unconstitutional, a union representing carriage operators and owners contend in a federal lawsuit filed Thursday seeking to block the measure.
items.body: (Bloomberg Law) -- New York City’s brand new law banning horse-drawn carriages is unconstitutional, a union representing carriage operators and owners contend in a federal lawsuit filed Thursday seeking to block the measure.The City Council-passed ban signed Thursday by Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) will phase out the 168-year-old industry before taking effect June 1, 2028 across all five boroughs. The law requires “humane disposition” of the horses, forbidding they be sold for slaughter or transferred to other carriage companies. Sixty-eight horse cabs currently operate in Central Park, employing roughly 200 drivers and up to 160 horses.The statute will “immediately cripple” carriage owners and ignore property interests and contracts, industry union Transport Workers Union Local 100 said in its class action complaint filed in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York.The union is seeking a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction blocking enforcement of the law until the court rules on the merits of the case. It’s also asking the court for expedited discovery.The city’s law department said it’s reviewing the case.The legislation, known as Romanch’s Law, passed following the death of 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan, who was killed over the summer after being thrown from a horse-drawn carriage in Central Park. The city has for decades tried to ban horse-drawn carriages — a Central Park tourist staple that’s been around since 1858.Just CompensationThe new law doesn’t include compensation for the property — such as permits and licenses, stables, and horses — that’s now rendered “unusable,” the complaint said. It only talks about a potential compensation plan that could come later down the road. That’s a violation of the US Constitution, which bars a “taking” without just compensation, the union alleges.It also “makes vague promises about a ‘transition plan’ that offers the carriage drivers affected only ‘help’ finding ‘employment opportunities,’” the complaint said.Mamdani at Thursday’s public signing ceremony said the city plans to release a transition plan in April that will including a process for the city to buy back medallions — operating licenses and plates — from owners, a stipend for drivers and stable hands to attend workforce training and career development classes, and career counseling and entrepreneurship support.The city will work directly with horse-carriage workers to receive and incorporate their feedback in the transition process, the mayor said. And the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene will oversee where each horse is sold or placed as they retire, he added.“This is a new day for our city — one that will make the crown jewel of Manhattan’s parks safer while also recognizing the lasting legacy and contributions the horse-carriage industry has made in our city,” Mamdani said.Advocates for Justice represents the Transport Workers Union.The case is Chiarello v. City of New York, S.D.N.Y., 1:26-cv-10154, complaint 11/19/26.To contact the reporters on this story: Beth Wang in New York City at bwang@bloombergindustry.com; Patricia Hurtado at pathurtado@bloomberg.netTo contact the editors responsible for this story: Carmen Castro-Pagán at ccastro-pagan@bloomberglaw.com; Andrew Harris at aharris@bloomberglaw.comMore stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.title: TD report examines financial health of Canadian households
items.author: Jordan Fleguel
items.summary: As Canadians grapple with elevated rates of unemployment and inflation, as well as the fallout from an ongoing trade war with the U.S., a new report suggests most households are still finding ways to ...
items.body: As Canadians grapple with elevated rates of unemployment and inflation, as well as the fallout from an ongoing trade war with the U.S., a new report suggests most households are still finding ways to make ends meet, despite a number of troubling economic data points. “Canadian consumers are holding up reasonably well,” wrote Maria Solovieva, CFA and economist, in a report released Thursday by TD Economics. The report noted that real consumer spending grew at a nearly three per cent pace through the first half of 2026, suggesting Canadians have remained resilient in the face of numerous economic challenges. “But solid spending growth masks pockets of financial strain, particularly in Ontario,” Solovieva wrote. “A closer look at several indicators – insolvencies, delinquencies, and mortgage arrears – reveals a mixed picture, with some measures showing signs of stabilizing while others continue to deteriorate.” Weakness in Ontario In Canada’s largest province, the current financial strain on Canadians is “most visible,” according to the report. “Ontario stands out with mortgage arrears nearly tripling from pre-pandemic norms and approaching their Global Financial Crisis (GFC) peak. This reflects elevated mortgage balances and greater sensitivity to borrowing costs,” it said. Mortgage arrears have also risen, to a lesser extent, in British Columbia, as both provinces experienced significant home price gains during the pandemic period, the report noted, leaving many homeowners with larger mortgage balances relative to income. While the pace of growth in B.C. mortgage arears has slowed more recently, the rate has continued to climb in Ontario, hitting 0.34 per cent in August. That’s nearly triple its pre-pandemic level of around 0.12 per cent and approaching the 0.43 per cent peak during the GFC, according to the report. “Still, perspective matters. Even at today’s elevated rate, roughly one in 300 Ontario mortgages is in arrears,” said Solovieva. “These missed payments do not necessarily translate into more severe financial distress or credit losses. Many borrowers retain substantial home equity, giving both households and lenders some flexibility to manage financial difficulties.” Those who are most vulnerable now are homeowners who purchased property during the 2021 and 2022 housing peak, when prices were highest and “equity cushions may be thinnest,” the report noted. Eyes on the labour market Across Canada, but particularly in Ontario, Canadians are faced with the combination of high living costs and a weakening labour market, which has hit some of the province’s traditional manufacturing centres hardest. “Notably, more than 35 per cent of people living in households in Oshawa, Windsor and Hamilton report difficulties meeting their financial needs – the highest among Canada’s largest cities,” wrote Solovieva. “Unemployment rates in all three cities are also above the national average, underscoring how labour market weakness is compounding existing affordability pressures in some regions.” At a national level, the labour market will continue to be a key indicator of the financial health of Canadians going forward, the report said. Earlier this month, Statistics Canada reported that the country’s unemployment rate rose to 6.7 per cent in October. It marked the third consecutive month of net job losses for the Canadian economy. ‘Little reason to sound the alarm’ TD says it expects stronger economic and labour market growth next year. However, forecasting accurately is difficult given the uncertainty surrounding Canada’s trading relationship with the U.S. as well as ongoing global conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. “Despite these vulnerabilities, we see little reason to sound the alarm bell over a broader deterioration in household credit performance. Ontario’s mortgage arrears are rising but are forecast to decline next year as the economy improves,” Solovieva argued. “If weak hiring gives way to widespread job losses… mortgage arrears could rise further and remain elevated for longer, but with stronger economic growth and a recovering labour market in our forecast, households in Ontario and across Canada are expected to bend but not break.”

FAST

Nov 19 : The US government was warned in a report it commissioned about major national security risks from weaknesses in the country's telecom networks in 2022, two years before sweeping Chinese-linked cyberespionage known as Salt Typhoon.
The report commissioned by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said US telecommunications networks contained "major structural vulnerabilities" and could be compromised from anywhere in the world.
US officials have previously alleged that hackers targeted nine telecom companies, including Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and Lumen, during the 2024 Salt Typhoon campaign and stole telephone audio intercepts and a large tranche of call-record data.
The report, disclosed as part of a lawsuit, has been reviewed by Reuters.

Details of the report were first reported by Bloomberg News on Thursday.
The June 2022 report described US telecom infrastructure as one in a "perilous and untenable situation," and added that international interconnects could provide attackers with "trusted" access. "The fact that US national networks can be readily compromised from anywhere in the world is not yet widely understood."
CISA withheld the report from public release for four years and resisted congressional pressure to publish it, according to Bloomberg News.
The agency did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Ron Wyden, a Democratic senator from Oregon, pushed for the release of the report last year. He had said in a statement, "Congress would have had ample time to require mandatory cybersecurity standards for phone companies, in time to prevent the Salt Typhoon hacks" had the report been made public when it was first written.

Bitcoin price ignores Anthropic debut as ANT share price dips below $100 1 min read

BTCUSD ANT
Bitcoin shrugged off US tech-stock strength at Thursday’s Wall Street open as markets reacted to Anthropic’s $111.50 debut.
Key points:
Anthropic opens at $111.50 per share on the Nasdaq, 34% above its IPO price of $83, rising as high as $115 before dropping to lows of $95.05.
Bitcoin (BTC) struggled to follow equities’ upside as sell-side pressure kept BTCUSD near four-month lows of $62,000.
Anthropic debut sees share price near 40% gain versus IPO
Data from TradingView showed BTCUSD falling to $62,250 as US stock markets headed higher.

BTCUSD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Excitement around Anthropic initially fueled 0.6% daily gains for the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index, which subsequently turned red on the day, down 1% at the time of writing. That followed 1.4% daily upside for South Korea’s tech-focused KOSPI Composite Index.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Trading of the company’s stock on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT began at $111.50, 34% above its IPO price of $83, reaching a local high of $115 before dropping below the $100 mark amid ongoing volatility.

Anthropic shares one-minute chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Perpetual futures traders on Hyperliquid had already placed fair value at around $103, based on a company valuation of around $1.845 trillion. Reacting, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter noted that the opening had pushed the valuation above $2 trillion, putting it in sixth place among the world’s most valuable public companies.
Previously, Cointelegraph reported on the record-breaking IPO helping to renew market trust in the AI sector amid ongoing uncertainty over Nvidia following the ousting of its CEO Jensen Huang.
“With some of the tumultuous times here for Nvidia, a little bit of that trust has gone away from the retail investor so this is the way people I think are going to express themselves,” J.J. Kinahan, senior vice president of retail and alternative investments at CBOE Global Markets, told CNBC.
In his latest analysis, economist Mohamed El-Erian called the IPO “historic.”
“On the micro side: In five years, it has gone from a startup to one of the world’s most valuable companies. It’s the largest IPO ever. On the macro side: Lots worth monitoring, starting with the flow-of-funds implications,” he summarized.

Nov 19 : Amazon said on Thursday that a New York City Council bill under consideration, requiring last-mile delivery operators to be licensed by the city and directly employ workers rather than contract the work, "could add up to $5" to each order.
The ecommerce major added that it might be forced to consider moving operations outside the city if the bill passes.
• Amazon told New York City customers that the council was weighing Intro 518, a bill sponsored by member Tiffany Caban, which could affect how it delivers packages and groceries and push prices up
• The company said it works with a network of small delivery businesses that it would no longer be able to work with if the legislation passes
• It also said moving operations outside the city would likely mean slower and more expensive deliveries for millions of customers
• "We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," Council Speaker Julie Menin told Reuters in a emailed statement, calling Amazon's campaign "deceptive"

Source: Reuters

items.summary: NVDA shares rose 4.63% to $157.95 at 9:45 a.m. ET on November 19 in regular trading, as Anthropic's final prospectus confirmed that Nvidia will buy 120,481,927 Class N shares for about $10.0 billion ...
items.body:

/ GuruFocus
/ Nvidia Stocks Rise 4.63% as $10 Billion Anthropic Stake Lands on IPO Day

Nvidia Stocks Rise 4.63% as $10 Billion Anthropic Stake Lands on IPO Day Less than 1 min read

NVDA ANT
Nvidia NVDA shares rose 4.63% to $157.95 at 9:45 a.m. ET on November 19 in regular trading, as Anthropic's final prospectus confirmed that Nvidia will buy 120,481,927 Class N shares for about $10.0 billion at the $83 IPO price. The bounce follows a rough week. Shares had dropped more than 13% over the past week after Jensen Huang's resignation, and new chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him.
The operating engine is not the problem. Third-quarter revenue reached $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, with a 74.8% GAAP gross margin and $2.70 of diluted EPS. Guidance calls for $130.0 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%, with no China data center compute revenue assumed. Nvidia returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter and still has about $227.3 billion left on its buyback authorization.

The $10 billion Anthropic cheque equals roughly 15% of last quarter's $65.3 billion net income, a manageable bet that also deepens ties with a key GPU customer. The GuruFocus page shows a GF Score of 91/100, built on near-perfect profitability and a fortress balance sheet. Yet the share price sits about 62% below the GF Value of $418.87, and GuruFocus flags a possible value trap. That gap suggests the market is pricing governance and China risk, not earnings. The next test is Huang's Capitol Hill appearances in December and whether hyperscaler orders hold under interim leadership.

/ GuruFocus
/ Broadcom Stocks Rise 4.21% as Chip Supplier Joins Anthropic's $26 Billion Placement

Broadcom Stocks Rise 4.21% as Chip Supplier Joins Anthropic's $26 Billion Placement Less than 1 min read

AVGO
Broadcom AVGO shares rose 4.21% to $368.96 at 9:45 a.m. ET on November 19 in regular trading, after Anthropic's final prospectus listed Broadcom among seven strategic buyers in a $26.0 billion private placement at the $83 IPO price. Broadcom will take 12,048,192 Class N shares for about $1.0 billion.
The filing describes Broadcom as both a supplier and a lessor to Anthropic, which runs a multi-chip setup across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs and AMD GPUs. Anthropic disclosed about $900.9 billion of aggregate committed spend on purchase commitments and leases, substantially all tied to compute. CNBC noted chipmakers broadly advanced before the listing.

A $1 billion stake is under 0.1% of Broadcom's $1.76 trillion market value, so the equity is a signal, not a profit driver. The real exposure is custom silicon and networking inside that $900.9 billion pipeline. GuruFocus rates Broadcom 98/100, with top profitability and strong value and growth readings. Shares trade about 19% below the GF Value of $454.06, which GuruFocus labels modestly undervalued. Broadcom's next quarterly report and its AI semiconductor revenue guidance will be the clearest read on that pipeline.

Nov 19 (Reuters) – Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office said on Thursday that the Wikimedia Foundation, which oversees Wikipedia and other information projects, could be branded undesirable under Russian law on grounds of destabilising the country.

A statement by the office, quoted by Interfax news agency, said it had issued a warning about the possibility of declaring Wikimedia undesirable.

“The Prosecutor General’s Office…has established facts that Wikimedia Foundation, Inc. is conducting a targeted information campaign to destabilise the situation on the territory of the Russian Federation,” the statement said.

Show Full Article

It said it had warned of punitive measures to be applied “in the instance that the destructive anti-Russian activity continues”.

The Wikimedia Foundation did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 

Russia regularly brands entities it says undermine its constitutional order or national security as “undesirable”. The law specifies prison terms of up to five years for funding such activity, or six years for organising it.

Wikipedia, a collaboratively edited encyclopedia, is one of the world’s most visited websites.

(Reporting by Reuters)

items.title: アンソロピック上場、17％高で終了　好評価持続できるか
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Niket Nishant　Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［１９日　ロイター］ - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックが１９日、ナスダック市場に新規上場した。主要ＡＩ開発企業としては世界初の上場となり、ＡＩブームの持続性を占う試金石として注目される中、時価総額は一時約２兆ドルに達した。市場関係者からは、この好評価を持続できるかが鍵との声が聞かれている。

初値は１１１．５ドルと、新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）価格の８３ドルを約３４％上回った。その後は上げ幅を縮小し、１７％高の９７．１７ドルで終了した。

アンソロピックはこれにより、時価総額「1兆ドルクラブ」入りし、マイクロソフトやアップル
items.body:
Niket Nishant　Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［１９日　ロイター］ - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックが１９日、ナスダック市場に新規上場した。主要ＡＩ開発企業としては世界初の上場となり、ＡＩブームの持続性を占う試金石として注目される中、時価総額は一時約２兆ドルに達した。市場関係者からは、この好評価を持続できるかが鍵との声が聞かれている。

初値は１１１．５ドルと、新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）価格の８３ドルを約３４％上回った。その後は上げ幅を縮小し、１７％高の９７．１７ドルで終了した。

アンソロピックはこれにより、時価総額「1兆ドルクラブ」入りし、マイクロソフトやアップル 、エヌビディアなどと肩を並べることになる。

アンソロピックの上場は、ＡＩ相場への熱狂が冷める中で実施された。関連企業の債務負担、米中間選挙での民主党圧勝を受けたデータセンター建設への逆風懸念、さらに１２日のエヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）退任が、ＡＩエコシステムを巡る懸念に拍車をかけた。

テクナリシス・リサーチのチーフアナリスト、ボブ・オドネル氏は「アンソロピックの大型上場は、ＡＩの可能性について市場を安心させる上で極めて重要な一歩だが、本当にまだ始まりにすぎない」と述べた。その上で「オープンＡＩがどうなるか、エヌビディアを巡る状況がどう展開するか、データセンターを巡る政治の風向きがどうなるか、そしてアンソロピックが実際にどのような実績を残すか。これらを見極めない限り、本当の意味で安定したとは言えない」と指摘した。

創業から６年のアンソロピックは、ＡＩの安全性を守る「門番」を自任してきた。同時に、巨額の計算コストを抱えながらも利益を出せると投資家に説明してきた。第３・四半期は、売上高が前期比で４７％増え、純損失は縮小した。ただ、成長のペースは前四半期から大きく鈍った。

アンソロピックは、債券市場での資金調達も視野に置く。ダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１９日、ＣＮＢＣのインタビューで「将来のある時点で投資適格の格付けを得たいと考えている。負債は当社が使える手段の一つで、将来のどこかで活用したい」と語った。

＜高い評価、維持できるか＞

指数リバランス分析会社イントロピックは、指数に連動するファンドのパッシブ需要により、２６年末までに売り出し株式の最大３０％が買われると推計する。

だが今後が「順風」とは言えない。ＡＩの「饗宴」はすでに冷めつつあり、成長持続に疑問符がついている。投資家の間では、上場直後の熱狂が収まるのを待ってから買うべきという声もある。

ＩＰＯＸのアソシエート、ルーカス・ミュールバウアー氏は、「需要の一部は、長期的な収益性が不透明であっても、有力なＡＩ企業への投資機会というまれなチャンスを逃したくない投資家心理を反映している」と指摘する。

ウェルス・コンサルティング・グループのチーフマーケットストラテジスト、タリー・レジェール氏は「市場のセンチメントに流されて割高な価格で購入することには賛成できない」と発言。個人投資家にとって「どんな価格でも買う機会ではない」と述べ、「過去の実績を見ると、人気の高いハイテク企業のＩＰＯ初日に購入した個人投資家は、３年間の投資期間で見ると、市場全体の指数をアンダーパフォームする傾向にある」と指摘した。

アンソロピックを「一芸に秀でた企業」と表現するＧＣＧアドバイザリー・パートナーズのパートナー、ビル・ガンダーソン氏は、「同社をアマゾンになぞらえる向きもあるが、アマゾンも数年間は赤字だった。しかし、アンソロピックにそれほどの時間的余裕はないだろう。早期の黒字化が求められる」と述べた。

最大の競合相手であるオープンＡＩは、早ければ２０２７年にも上場を目指しているとみられている。

＜従業員には大きな報酬＞

ＩＰＯでは約８１０億ドルを調達し、６月に上場した米宇宙企業スペースＸの７５０億ドルを上回って過去最大のＩＰＯとなった。

主幹事証券会社が追加株式購入オプションを全額行使した場合、調達額は最大９３５億ドルに達する可能性がある。

また、私募を通じて調達した２６０億ドルを含めると、調達総額は１０７０億ドルを超える。私募の投資家には、AMD、 ブロードコム、アルファベット 傘下のグーグル、マイクロン、マイクロソフト、エヌビディア、TSMCが含まれる。 規制当局への提出文書によると、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが率いる引受団は、約５億５０００万ドルの手数料を得る見込み。

また今回のＩＰＯにより、アンソロピックの現・元従業員の間で数千人の「ペーパーミリオネア（含み資産ベースの百万長者）」が誕生する見通しだ。また、ＩＰＯ価格に基づくロイターの試算では、同社株式の約１０％を共同で保有するアモデイＣＥＯら共同創業者７人の保有株式の価値は１５００億ドル近くに達する。

Musk's SpaceXSI denies liability in UK lawmaker's lawsuit over Grok images

A 3D-printed miniature model of Elon Musk and Grok logo are seen in this illustration taken, February 16, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

LONDON, Nov 19 : Elon Musk's SpaceXSI has filed its defence against a British lawmaker's lawsuit over fake images of her created using the Grok AI platform, arguing that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach someone's right to privacy.
Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party who has publicly criticised both Musk and Grok, is suing after users generated sexualised images of her, including a video of her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault".
In its written defence, dated October 29, SpaceXSI, part of Musk's SpaceX, denies liability for any alleged breach of Asato's privacy or data protection rights.
Asato filed her lawsuit at London's High Court for misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws, alleging the way Grok was designed and trained enabled it to generate sexualised content.

The company's defence, in one of the first claims to test liability for the design of an AI system, could provide an insight into how designers may contest similar lawsuits.
Lawyers for SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC said it had removed AI-generated images of Asato that breached its terms, including the video depicting Asato being chloroformed.
They argued, however, that other images it allowed to remain available "would be understood by reasonable and sensible persons viewing that content to be AI-generated, fictitious and implausible ... rather than as realistic images", meaning Asato has no reasonable expectation of privacy.
SpaceXSI also argues it did not breach Asato's data protection rights, including because it "did not determine the content of the relevant users' prompts".
LAWMAKER SAYS PLATFORMS SHOULD BE ACCOUNTABLE
Asato said in a statement on Thursday that those building powerful AI tools must take responsibility.
"SpaceX SI wants to have it both ways," Asato said. 
"The company admits it built the AI model, rewrote user requests to add its own graphic details, pulled images from across the internet, and published the results from an account it controls," she said, adding: "Yet it also claims it is a neutral bystander without legal responsibility".
Asato is seeking a court order requiring SpaceXSI, which was formerly called xAI and then SpaceXAI, to "implement effective and permanent technical measures" to ensure Grok cannot create manipulated images of her.
SpaceXSI says she is not entitled to such an order. 
Grok, which is distributed through social media platform X, is subject to regulatory probes in several countries after an outcry over its use to create non-consensual sexualised images.
In mid-January, xAI said it restricted image editing in Grok and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing "where it's illegal". 
But Reuters found in early February that, even after new curbs, Grok continued to generate sexualised images of people even when users explicitly warned the subjects did not consent. X and xAI did not address detailed questions from Reuters about Grok's generation of sexualised material.
In July, xAI sued a man in the US alleging he misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material, in one of the first cases of its kind brought by an AI company.

Nov 19 : Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" is set to help Take-Two Interactive, the publisher of the blockbuster game that is now a global cultural phenomenon, rake in more than $2 billion in estimated first-day sales.
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, is not a household name despite its portfolio of massive hits including the "Red Dead Redemption" franchise and the "NBA 2K" basketball series.
Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates total units sold at 24.58 million, as of Thursday evening, translating to about $2.36 billion in revenue for Take-Two. That is almost three times the roughly $800 million worth of copies GTA V sold on its first day in 2013, widely regarded as the best-selling videogame in the first 24 hours.
Meanwhile, Take-Two has remained tight-lipped about GTA VI demand since it opened for pre-orders in June, limiting commentary to saying demand has been "unprecedented" or "far exceeding expectations."

"The title is so widely anticipated, consumers appear very, very excited, and all the press so far has been universally positive, but we still aren't ready to declare victory," CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Take-Two's earnings call earlier this month.
"We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs."
GTA VI MARKETING BLITZ
Take-Two has shelled out an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs for GTA VI, making it one of the most expensive entertainment projects.
Sensor Tower estimates that the game's promotional trailer, GTA VI "Extended Look", on Netflix in August helped drive a sixfold jump in pre-orders.
In Miami, which Vice City is based on, the city's NBA team celebrated the release on Wednesday with a Vice City-themed match.
Over the weekend, the company is hosting "GTA VI: The Festival" - a music show with a star-studded line-up that includes Grammy-winning rapper Cardi B, hip hop record producer Metro Boomin and rapper Travis Scott.
WHAT NEXT FOR TAKE-TWO?
Investors have been waiting to hear from Take-Two about its plans for a PC launch of GTA VI and an online version rollout. The online, multiplayer component of a videogame is crucial in turning the title into a recurring revenue engine.
Some industry analysts are expecting the PC launch and online mode in 2027.
Brokerage TD Cowen named Take-Two one of its 'Best Ideas' for 2027, with its analyst Doug Creutz upbeat about the company's financial prospects when the game releases online.
"The potential ceiling for GTA VI's long-term recurrent consumer spending performance is very high... 'when' and 'how big' the next GTA Online will be is the most important question for the stock, more so than GTA VI unit sales."

Stocks fall as Anthropic debut fails to ease AI concerns

Despite Anthropic’s stock closing up 17 per cent on its debut, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite all fell at least 2 per cent.
